title: The monsters with a trick of their own
target: The monsters in R.E.P.O. that each do one unusual thing: balloons as a weapon, a laser rather than a grab, two bodies in one, a spotlight instead of eyes, hands you hear coming, and a tongue that takes your head.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A level that has one of these monsters in it
A crew that calls out what it can see
A route with more than one way out of the room

steps.do: Do not read the balloons around a monster as decoration.
steps.because: it keeps a maximum number of balloons, a prefab and the points they spawn at, and it has a state for blowing one up (maxBalloons, balloonPrefab, balloonSpawnPoints, blowing)

steps.do: Expect a popped balloon to be an event of its own.
steps.because: a balloon popping has an effect of its own, and the monster checks collisions for a balloon, for standing up and for a door (balloonPopEffect, balloonCollisionChecker, standUpCollisionChecker, doorCollisionChecker)

steps.do: Expect the tall one with the nose to shoot rather than to grab.
steps.because: the beamer has a laser with a start point and a ray of its own, and its aim uses a vertical transform with a curve, a spread and a speed (laser, laserStartTransform, laserRayTransform, aimVerticalTransform, aimHorizontalSpread, aimHorizontalSpeed)

steps.do: Treat a heart hugger as more than one monster, because it has more than one body.
steps.because: it has a set of normal meshes and a set of horror meshes, each kept as lists with a base scale and a target (normalMesh1, normalMesh2, horrorMesh1, horrorMesh2, meshTransforms, cuteMeshTransforms)

steps.do: Listen for its gas before you ever see the second face.
steps.because: its gas has a start, a tell and a stop, and it has a gas checker, gas particles and a loop of its own (soundGasStart, soundGasTell, soundGasStop, gasChecker, gasParticles, soundGasLoop)

steps.do: Understand that the oogly sees with a light rather than with eyes.
steps.because: it sees with a spotlight and a point light of its own, with a maximum intensity (visionTransform, visionSpotlight, visionPointLight, pointLightMaxIntensity)

steps.do: Stay out of its cone rather than merely out of its sight.
steps.because: the spotlight fades in and out on its own curves and durations, and it has sounds for switching on and off (animationCurveSpotlightIntro, animationCurveSpotlightOutro, spotlightIntroDuration, spotlightOutroDuration, audioSpotlightOn, audioSpotlightOff)

steps.do: Listen for a robed monster's hands, because they are audible on their own.
steps.because: its hands have an idle sound and an aggressive one, each with a flag for whether it is playing, and it has an attack from underneath as well as an ordinary one (sfxHandIdle, sfxHandAggressive, sfxAttack, sfxAttackUnder, sfxAttackUnderGlobal)

steps.do: Know that its eye is placed on its own rather than set in a head.
steps.because: its eye has a location of its own, it turns on a rotation spring, and its end piece trails on a spring with a source and a target (eyeLocation, rotationSpring, endPieceSpring, endPieceSource, endPieceTarget)

steps.do: Expect the last one to come at your head rather than your body.
steps.because: its head, torso and tongue hang on springs with sources and targets, and the tongue keeps separate middle and tip parts (springHeadTalk, springTorsoTalk, springTongueMiddle, springTongueTip, springTongueMiddleTransform, springTongueTipTarget)

steps.do: Listen for the grab and the release, because both are sounded.
steps.because: grabbing a head and releasing it each have their own sound, and the release has a start and an end (soundGrabHead, soundReleaseHeadStart, soundReleaseHeadEnd)

steps.do: Read its dropkick before it lands, because it is staged.
steps.because: a dropkick is staged in four sounds: a tell, a start, an end and a hit (soundDropkickTell, soundDropkickStart, soundDropkickEnd, soundDropkickHit)

commonMistakes: Walking through a room full of balloons as if they were scenery.
Treating the beamer's nose as a face rather than as an aiming rig.
Meeting a heart hugger's cute form and assuming that is the whole monster.
Standing in the oogly's light because nothing has looked at you yet.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
